name: lens-reader
description: The /lens Reader lens: a third-party extractor's opinion of a page, served from its own Worker so the site bundle never carries a DOM.
$comment: Every wrangler script passes -c wrangler.toml EXPLICITLY. Without it wrangler walks UP the tree, finds the ROOT wrangler.jsonc, and runs its build.command (`node tools/build.ts`) from this directory, dying with MODULE_NOT_FOUND on a file that only exists at the repo root. CI's steps for cf-garage and lwe-ask have always passed -c for that reason, so the flag looks like ceremony until you drop it: `pnpm run deploy` then fails in a way no CI run can catch, because CI never invokes these scripts.
$comment:htmlparser2-override: linkedom 0.18.13 declares htmlparser2 ^10.1.0, whose v5/v3/v2 DOM stack duplicates the v6/v4/v3 stack linkedom already gets through css-select. The override removes those duplicate entity tables and, more importantly, makes the parity oracle in test/dom-differential.test.mjs resolve the SAME parser src/dom.ts bundles: a gate whose reference parses differently proves nothing. Measured on the v11 override: 113.30 -> 80.56 KiB gzip (28.9% less), byte-identical output on a fixed four-page corpus, no measurable conversion regression. THIS COMMENT ARGUED FOR v11 AND AGAINST v12 UNTIL 2026-08-24, and the reversal is worth reading rather than deleting. It said v12 is NOT interchangeable because its WHATWG raw-text change breaks linkedom's self-closing-script serialization in linkedom's upstream suite. That is true of the suite and silent on which parse is RIGHT, which is the question a lens showing what a machine saw actually has. Chrome 148.0.7778.280 sides with v12 on all three behaviours that separate the versions and with v11 on none: a self-closing <script/> swallows to the next close tag, <?> is a bogus comment rather than nothing, and SVG clipPath keeps its case. So linkedom's upstream test pins the pre-spec string, as this project's own test did. Taking v12 left the Markdown byte-identical on 10 of 10 captured pages and dom-differential at 4 of 4. Keep the override at whatever version is pinned above; the tests derive it rather than restating it. Re-evaluate, do not carry blindly, when linkedom changes its parser range.

scripts.comment:typecheck: Runs from HERE rather than from the root `typecheck` script, because this project is deliberately out of the workspace and readability/linkedom live in lens-reader/node_modules. Wired into the root script instead, CI fails with TS2307 on both imports while every workstation that has run an install here stays green, which is the split CLAUDE.md records about the root contract suite arriving through a second door. tsc itself comes from the root install; only the dependency graph is local. The test suite is a SECOND program (config/tsconfig.lens-reader-test.json) because it runs on node while src/ runs on workerd, and it goes through check-test-types.mjs rather than tsc directly: importing ../src/reader.js pulls the Worker's crawl.ts in against node globals, and those diagnostics are missing declarations rather than findings.

$comment:dom: linkedom is a DEV dependency now. src/dom.ts is a first-party DOM over the same htmlparser2 linkedom wrapped, fitted to the 39 members Readability touches and the 11 reader.ts touches. linkedom stays installed as the ORACLE for test/dom-differential.test.mjs, which holds the fitted DOM to it byte-for-byte across 48 documents and asserts an identical parse tree on the 10 captured real-world pages. Deleting linkedom outright would delete the only thing that can prove the replacement is faithful. Measured 2026-08-23 on the swap: 80.57 -> 46.18 KiB gzip (42.7% less) and, over nine alternating trials on a 5754 KiB corpus, a 614.5 -> 299.4 ms median for the full parse-extract-markdown pipeline (51.3% less CPU, 12.80 -> 6.24 ms/doc).
